subject: Daily AcreetionOS Update -- September 18, 2026
body:
Daily AcreetionOS Update - September 18, 2026

Dear AcreetionOS Community,

As we continue to work towards our goal of creating a user-friendly, community-driven Linux distribution based on Arch Linux, we're excited to share some recent developments with you. Our community has been actively engaged, and we're grateful for the contributions and feedback we've received.

In the past week, we've seen the release of GNOME 51, which brings several performance improvements and new features to the desktop environment. We're keeping an eye on this development, and we're considering how we can incorporate these updates into our own distribution.

In terms of security, we've issued updates for various packages, including .NET, kernel, and firewalld. These updates are essential for maintaining the security and stability of our system, and we recommend that all users apply them as soon as possible.

On the development front, we've made several commits to our codebase. These changes include updates to our CI/CD pipeline, fixes for release.yml, and the addition of a new package, firefox-ublock-origin, to our Xlibre build. We're also working on re-triggering our GitLab mirror and ensuring that our scripts are properly linted.

One of the most significant changes we've made recently is the merge of the main branch into the release-1 branch in AcreetionOS-Xlibre. This update resolves a conflict with geocode-glib and ensures that our Xlibre build remains stable and up-to-date.

We're also excited to announce that our community has been actively contributing to our wiki guides and newsletter. These efforts will help us better document our project and keep our community informed about the latest developments.

As we move forward, we're committed to transparency and open communication. We encourage all community members to participate in our discussions and contribute to our project in any way they can. Whether it's through code contributions, documentation, or simply providing feedback, your input is invaluable to us.

We're proud of the progress we've made so far, and we're excited to see where this journey takes us. Thank you for being part of the AcreetionOS community, and we look forward to continuing to work together to create a better, more user-friendly Linux distribution.

If you have any questions or concerns, please don't hesitate to reach out to us. We're always here to help. You can find us on our Discord server, where we're actively engaged with the community and happy to answer any questions you may have.

Best regards,
Natalie Cole-Clift Spiva and Darren Clift, Co-Lead Developers of AcreetionOS
